newsitem.title: INDIA: India's PM says no plan now to raise petro prices.
newsitem.headline: India's PM says no plan now to raise petro prices.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda was quoted on Monday as saying the government has no intention as of now to raise the prices of petroleum products.
"As of now, the United Front government has no intention to take such a step," United News of India (UNI) quoted the prime minister as saying.

Deve Gowda, who was speaking in his southern state of Karnataka, was responding to speculation in newspapers that his United Front coalition was considering raising the prices of petroleum products to curb burgeoning subsidies.

UNI quoted the prime minister as saying his government had come to power at a time of mounting petroleum subsidies, and the ruling coalition had responded by increasing prices shortly after taking office in June.
